I feel the pain. But I live in Korea, which has been getting plenty of events which are fairly rare on English-speaking trade areas, so it's not so bad for me.

I live in China so I am completely screwed... People are into pokemon here for sure, but we have no official recognition from Nintendo and we can never hope to see an actual event, Chinese or English; I think the reasoning is very political because of all of the vitriol between China and Japan.

Thankfully it's not like that here. There's a lot of anti-Japanese sentiment here too; they had bans on a lot of Japanese cultural goods until as recently as 2002 here (even last year a song was banned by a broadcast station for having "Pika" in the lyrics). It's difficult for me, as someone who loves Japan, has studied in Japan, and traveled to Japan many times. I can understand the reasons for the sentiment (even if not as well as Koreans who were more directly affected by the history), Japan did some pretty terrible things, but it still puts me in awkward situations a lot of times. When Koreans find out I've studied in Japan/traveled to Japan, a lot of times they try to bring me into the dispute, ask me "Is Dokdo Korean or Japanese!?" etc. etc....

I moved to Beijing a few years ago and there is a bit of anti-Japanese sentiment that is noticeable if you know where to look. In 2012 their were small scale riots in the city with people throwing bricks through Japanese restaurant windows, tipping over Japanese cars, and forcing a closure of the Japanese embassy. People were putting signs on their business's windows which read stuff like "No Japanese or Dogs Allowed"; all kinds of dumb shit like that...

The Chinese still feel deeply wronged by the invasion during WWII, even many of the younger generations, because the people that fought the Japanese are still alive, so they are able to feed into an anti-Japanese mentality. My wife's grandpa fought them in Hong Kong and Guangdong, her great uncles did the same, so she grew up hearing about what happened straight from the horse's mouth. She isn't crazy about though, she likes Japanese culture, food and products and we are seriously considering moving there at the end of the year, amongst other places.

I love the culture and the food, as well. And my favorite living novelist is Haruki Murakami, whose work I love dearly. I also grew up on Japanese video games, like Zelda and Pokemon!

• 1 can Chipotle pepper in Adobo
  • 1/2 to 3/4 can. Can is large flat and round. Guava Paste.
  • Onions
  • Garlic
  • Beer
  • Large can tomatoes or 2 to 3 10 oz cans
  • 1/4 C Molasses
  • 1 to 2 cups fresh Lime Juice
  • 1/8 C Red Wine Vin.

  • Cilantro

  • Sauté Onions, Garlic until brown.

  • Deglaze 1 bottle of good beer.
  • Reduce until alcohol has burned off.
  • Add in Guava, Tomatoes, Lime Juice, Molasses
  • Reduce on medium heat for an hour.
  • Cool a bit, add chopped cilantro.
  • Let set for 10 mins to get flavor of cilantro into mix.
  • Run through china cap to remove veggie matter
  • Make sure the sauce can coat back of spoon, or thicker
  • if not think enough reduce longer
  • Salt, pepper, add acid (lime juice, red wine vin) to taste.
